audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] is marked Akshan 3/10 but its why reads "Maximum Dosage makes you nearly unkillable in long fights. The lane flips from 'survive' to 'walk at him' the moment you hit 6" — the stage text argues the opposite of its own side field. tldr is also truncated mid-sentence, ending in a stray "Dr.".
audit.why: Comeuppance (100/85/70s) deals damage based on missing health, so Level 6 genuinely is Akshan's window against a bar he has been chipping all lane. The content layer (win[4] = Akshan, whys[4]) and the packet level chart both agree; only the full-layer prose disagreed.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten to the Akshan side: Comeuppance's missing-health scaling, and pressing R before taking the fight rather than after.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike gave no number for Comeuppance and never connected it to Maximum Dosage.
audit.why: Comeuppance scales on the target's missing health while Akshan stores bullets; Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of missing health. Pressing R BEFORE he releases removes most of the damage — pressing it after is too late. The mirror audit records this same instant-heal correction from Akshan's side, so both pages now state it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and mid now carry the missing-health scaling and the sequencing (R first, then fight).

audit.whatIsWrong: TWO FABRICATIONS. (1) Five fields give Dr. Mundo an "E stun": whys[2], spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text, mid ("E (Blunt Force Trauma) stuns his grapple") and wants.you[0] ("E-stun him mid-grapple"). Blunt Force Trauma has no stun — it is a bag slam dealing missing-health damage that swats away enemies it kills. (2) Six fields say Infected Bonesaw gives a "slow + HP refund": tradeGood, phases[2].why, breakdown.early, breakdown.trading, report[3].t and dosFull[1].d. Riot's description is damage based on current health plus a slow — there is no heal on the Q at all. Separately, three fields build advice around the passive cannister (tradeBad, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[0].t) when Akshan has no immobilising effect anywhere in his kit, so Goes Where He Pleases never fires in this lane.
audit.why: The real interactions, all from Riot's own text: Heroic Swing (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s) says he "gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain" — walking into his swing path drops him out of it, which is the actual answer to his escape, not a stun he can dodge. Comeuppance "deal[s] damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit", so a minion between you and him eats the whole ult. Avengerang "deals damage going out and coming back", so the return, not the throw, is the hit to sidestep. Infected Bonesaw scales on CURRENT health, which inverts the advice — it hits hardest while Akshan is healthy, not when he is low. Heart Zapper (17/16.5/16/15.5/15s) stores a portion of the damage you take and heals a percentage of it on the burst, so his poke during W funds your health bar; the mirror records this as the decisive interaction of the matchup.
audit.corrected: See edits — stun removed from all five fields, Q heal removed from all six, cannister framing replaced with the Heroic Swing collision rule and the Comeuppance minion block.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t both track Heroic Swing with no number and describe it only as a "dash + camera swing escape".
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s and Avengerang 9/8/7/6/5s. The swing breaks on champion collision, which is a far more useful fact than its cooldown alone.
audit.corrected: Numbers added, collision rule stated, and the third bullet turned into the Avengerang return.

notes: Two separate fabrications, each repeated across many fields. (1) The "E stun" again — five fields told the player to stun Akshan out of his grapple with Blunt Force Trauma. Mundo has no stun; the ability that actually breaks Heroic Swing is your own body, because Riot's text says he "gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain". (2) "Q cleaver for the slow + HP refund" in six fields — Infected Bonesaw has no heal in Riot's description, only current-health damage and a slow. The heal in Mundo's kit is Heart Zapper's stored-damage payback. Also removed three fields built on the passive cannister: Akshan's kit contains no immobilising effect at all, so Goes Where He Pleases never triggers in this lane and per the relevance rule I wrote nothing about the passive in their place. tldr was truncated on disk, ending in a stray "Dr." — repaired. Two more Riot-text interactions that were absent everywhere and are now stated: Comeuppance stops on the first champion, MINION or structure hit (a minion body-blocks the whole ult), and Avengerang damages going out AND coming back, so the return is the hit to sidestep. Per the mirror's caution, I did not repeat the _missing file's "Maximum Dosage bypasses stacking resistances" rule — Riot's text describes a heal with no resistance interaction.
